name: Silent Beacon
description: A normal-difficulty SOC investigation scenario focused on detecting DNS beaconing from a compromised internal workstation, tracing internal reconnaissance, identifying data staging on a file server, and applying coordinated containment before full exfiltration occurs.

global_design_notes.scenario_focus: Network-focused SOC investigation of DNS beaconing, workstation persistence, LDAP-style internal reconnaissance, SMB/data staging, and final containment.
global_design_notes.controlled_variation_note: Future variants may swap the compromised workstation, C2 domain, target share, decoy node, and timing profile while keeping scoring and correctness deterministic.
global_design_notes.ai_support_note: Future AI support may rewrite alerts, logs, hints, mentor notifications, and report feedback, but deterministic scenario logic controls correctness, scoring, progression, and approved variants.
global_design_notes.scoring_note: Final scoring should consider base action score, investigation coverage, sequence quality, time efficiency, wrong action penalties, timeout/escalation penalty, premature containment penalty, response quality, and wrong abstraction-level action penalties.

stages.name: Suspicious DNS Beaconing
stages.learning_objective: Validate the DNS beaconing path by correlating DNS-SRV, the suspicious external C2 domain, and the source workstation before applying a DNS/perimeter block.

time_pressure.timeout_warning: Time pressure is increasing. The DNS beacon pattern is still active and may continue receiving commands.
time_pressure.timeout_mentor_feedback: Delayed DNS investigation allowed the beacon to keep communicating with the suspicious domain.
time_pressure.timeout_log_message: TIMEOUT: DNS beaconing continued long enough for the attacker to prepare internal reconnaissance.

extra_logs.message: DNS: Continued TXT queries from WS-SALES-01 preceded suspicious scheduled task activity.

next_stage_modifier.mentor_context: Because the DNS beacon was not triaged quickly, the workstation activity stage begins with elevated attacker momentum.

events.message: DNS: WS-SALES-01 issued repeated TXT queries to random subdomains of update-check.ddns.net at near-regular intervals
FIREWALL: Outbound traffic from WS-SALES-01 is almost entirely DNS while query volume exceeds workstation baseline
Possible DNS beaconing path detected through DNS-SRV toward update-check.ddns.net

stages.mentor_hint: Start with DNS-SRV and the external C2 domain. This stage is about validating and disrupting the DNS path, not host isolation.

mentor.stage_hint: Select DNS-SRV first, review the DNS query pattern, then validate the suspicious external domain and source workstation before blocking.
mentor.coverage_incomplete: The DNS path is not fully validated yet. Inspect DNS-SRV, the external C2 domain, and WS-SALES-01 before response.
mentor.wrong_order: Blocking before validating the DNS path may stop traffic but weakens the investigation record.
mentor.premature_response: A DNS block is useful only after confirming that the queries behave like beaconing rather than normal resolution.
mentor.correct_sequence: Good sequence. You validated the DNS source, path, and suspicious domain before disrupting the beacon path.
mentor.timeout_warning: Time pressure is increasing. The beacon may continue receiving commands through DNS.
mentor.timeout_feedback: The delay allowed DNS beaconing to persist and increased the likelihood of internal activity.

correct.mentor_feedback: The suspicious DNS path was investigated and disrupted before the beacon could continue unnoticed.
correct.log_message: DNS-SRV and external C2 path validated; suspicious DNS beacon path blocked.

wrong.mentor_feedback: Unresolved DNS beaconing allows the attacker to continue command-and-control communication using an allowed protocol.
wrong.log_message: DNS beaconing remains active from WS-SALES-01.

ai_metadata.stage_objective: Validate the DNS beaconing path by correlating DNS-SRV, the suspicious external C2 domain, and the source workstation before applying a DNS/perimeter block.

facts.label: Repeated DNS TXT-style queries suggest a beaconing pattern.
The suspicious external domain must be validated before blocking.
The DNS control point is part of the containment path.

stages.name: Compromised Workstation Activity
stages.learning_objective: Confirm workstation compromise by reviewing WS-SALES-01 user context, scheduled task creation, and encoded PowerShell activity before host containment.

time_pressure.timeout_warning: Time pressure is increasing. Persistence activity may allow the beacon to survive simple disruption.
time_pressure.timeout_mentor_feedback: Delayed host investigation allowed the suspicious scheduled task to remain active.
time_pressure.timeout_log_message: TIMEOUT: Scheduled task persistence remained active on WS-SALES-01.

extra_logs.message: LDAP: Suspicious domain enumeration began after unresolved scheduled task activity on WS-SALES-01.

next_stage_modifier.mentor_context: Because workstation persistence was not contained quickly, internal reconnaissance begins with stronger compromise evidence.

events.message: WINDOWS: Event 4698 scheduled task SoftwareUpdateTask created by CORP\jsmith on WS-SALES-01
PROCESS: powershell.exe launched with encoded command by Task Scheduler on WS-SALES-01
Suspicious scheduled task and encoded PowerShell activity detected on WS-SALES-01

stages.mentor_hint: This is the host-compromise stage. Focus on WS-SALES-01 user/process evidence before isolation.

mentor.stage_hint: Select WS-SALES-01 and inspect scheduled task, encoded PowerShell, and user context before isolating the host.
mentor.coverage_incomplete: Host compromise is not fully validated yet. Review identity, activity, and interpretation evidence on the workstation.
mentor.wrong_order: Isolating before reviewing host activity can stop the machine but leave persistence and user context unexplained.
mentor.premature_response: Containment should follow after you understand what task or process created the suspicious activity.
mentor.correct_sequence: Good sequence. You reviewed user and host activity before containing the compromised workstation.
mentor.timeout_warning: Time pressure is increasing. Persistence may continue to run if the host is not contained.
mentor.timeout_feedback: The delay allowed the scheduled task to keep supporting attacker activity.

correct.mentor_feedback: The suspicious scheduled task and encoded PowerShell activity were investigated before workstation containment.
correct.log_message: WS-SALES-01 isolated after host compromise validation.

wrong.mentor_feedback: Failure to validate and contain the workstation lets persistence continue and supports internal reconnaissance.
wrong.log_message: Scheduled task persistence remains active on WS-SALES-01.

ai_metadata.stage_objective: Confirm workstation compromise by reviewing WS-SALES-01 user context, scheduled task creation, and encoded PowerShell activity before host containment.

facts.label: The workstation activity needs confirmation before host containment.
Suspicious execution-style activity supports workstation compromise.
Containment should target the confirmed compromised workstation, not a decoy asset.

stages.name: Internal Reconnaissance
stages.learning_objective: Investigate DC-01 as the target of internal reconnaissance and confirm the workstation-to-domain-controller query path before containment.

time_pressure.timeout_warning: Time pressure is increasing. The attacker may use internal reconnaissance results to select a data target.
time_pressure.timeout_mentor_feedback: Delayed internal reconnaissance response allowed the attacker to map domain resources.
time_pressure.timeout_log_message: TIMEOUT: Internal enumeration completed and attacker knowledge of file-server access increased.

extra_logs.message: SMB: HR share access followed unresolved internal reconnaissance from WS-SALES-01.

next_stage_modifier.mentor_context: Because internal reconnaissance was not investigated quickly, data staging begins with higher risk.

events.message: DIRECTORY: WS-SALES-01 generated high-volume LDAP-style queries for users, groups, and service accounts against DC-01
DNS: TXT beacon query from WS-SALES-01 preceded internal enumeration activity by less than one minute
Possible automated internal reconnaissance detected against DC-01 from WS-SALES-01

stages.mentor_hint: This stage is about DC-01 being queried abnormally. Focus on the domain controller and directory-query evidence before disrupting the reconnaissance path.

mentor.stage_hint: Select DC-01 first and inspect activity/connectivity evidence. Then confirm WS-SALES-01 as the source of enumeration.
mentor.coverage_incomplete: Internal reconnaissance is not fully validated yet. Review connectivity, activity, and interpretation for DC-01 and WS-SALES-01.
mentor.wrong_order: Containment before tracing the internal query path may hide how the attacker selected later targets.
mentor.premature_response: Blocking internal traffic too early can disrupt investigation and normal domain services.
mentor.correct_sequence: Good sequence. You traced the internal reconnaissance path before containment.
mentor.timeout_warning: Time pressure is increasing. Reconnaissance data may help the attacker choose a file server target.
mentor.timeout_feedback: The delay allowed domain enumeration to complete and increased data-staging risk.

correct.mentor_feedback: The domain-controller reconnaissance activity was investigated and disrupted before it could fully support staging.
correct.log_message: DC-01 reconnaissance evidence validated; suspicious directory-query activity disrupted.

wrong.mentor_feedback: Missed internal reconnaissance allows the attacker to map accounts, groups, and likely data locations.
wrong.log_message: Domain enumeration from WS-SALES-01 continues toward DC-01.

ai_metadata.stage_objective: Investigate DC-01 as the target of internal reconnaissance and confirm the workstation-to-domain-controller query path before containment.

facts.label: Internal query activity suggests reconnaissance toward a sensitive internal service.
The path between the workstation and domain controller should be validated.
Response should follow confirmation of the internal reconnaissance target.

stages.name: File Server Data Staging
stages.learning_objective: Investigate FS-01 as the sensitive data source and confirm suspicious HR share access plus archive staging before containment.

time_pressure.timeout_warning: Time pressure is increasing. Staged data may be prepared for outbound transfer.
time_pressure.timeout_mentor_feedback: Delayed staging response allowed sensitive files to be collected into an archive.
time_pressure.timeout_log_message: TIMEOUT: Staged archive remained available to the attacker and exfiltration risk increased.

extra_logs.message: NETWORK: Staged archive on WS-SALES-01 is ready for outbound transfer through the active beacon channel.

next_stage_modifier.mentor_context: Because data staging was not contained quickly, the final containment stage begins with elevated exfiltration risk.

events.message: SMB: CORP\jsmith accessed \\FS-01\HR$ from WS-SALES-01 outside normal business activity
PROCESS: 7z.exe created HR_Backup_Q2.zip on WS-SALES-01 after HR share access
Possible sensitive data staging detected on FS-01 from WS-SALES-01 activity

stages.mentor_hint: This stage is about staged data on the file server. Focus on file access and archive creation before containment.

mentor.stage_hint: Select FS-01 first and inspect file-share activity. Then confirm WS-SALES-01 as the staging host.
mentor.coverage_incomplete: Data staging is not fully validated yet. Review identity, activity, and interpretation evidence for FS-01 and WS-SALES-01.
mentor.wrong_order: Containment before staging validation can stop the host but leave data exposure scope unclear.
mentor.premature_response: Isolating too early may protect the network but weakens evidence about which files were accessed.
mentor.correct_sequence: Good sequence. You validated file access and archive creation before containment.
mentor.timeout_warning: Time pressure is increasing. Staged data may be exfiltrated if the beacon remains active.
mentor.timeout_feedback: The delay allowed staged data to remain available for outbound transfer.

correct.mentor_feedback: Sensitive file access and archive creation on the file server were investigated before containment.
correct.log_message: FS-01 sensitive share access validated; staged archive path interrupted.

wrong.mentor_feedback: Failure to validate data staging leaves the organization unsure which files were accessed and whether exfiltration is imminent.
wrong.log_message: Staged archive remains on the compromised workstation.

ai_metadata.stage_objective: Investigate FS-01 as the sensitive data source and confirm suspicious HR share access plus archive staging before containment.

facts.label: Suspicious access to a sensitive share suggests possible data staging.
Archive or volume indicators should be validated before containment.
The data source and staging location should both be confirmed.

stages.name: C2 Blocking and Host Containment
stages.learning_objective: Apply coordinated containment by validating the external C2 domain, DNS control point, compromised workstation, and staged data risk before blocking the malicious DNS path.

time_pressure.timeout_warning: Time pressure is critical. If containment is delayed, staged data may leave the network.
time_pressure.timeout_mentor_feedback: Delayed containment allowed exfiltration risk to increase and produced a degraded scenario outcome.
time_pressure.timeout_log_message: TIMEOUT: C2 remained active long enough for probable data-loss exposure.

final_outcome_modifier.mentor_context: The campaign ended with degraded containment because C2 blocking and host containment were not completed in time.

events.message: DNS: Beacon from WS-SALES-01 remains active and is requesting transfer instructions from update-check.ddns.net
DLP: Staged archive HR_Backup_Q2.zip is present on WS-SALES-01 but no confirmed outbound archive transfer has completed yet
Critical containment window: validate external C2, DNS-SRV, WS-SALES-01, and FS-01 before final block

stages.mentor_hint: This final stage is about validating the active DNS C2 path and staged data exposure before containment. Focus on DNS-SRV, the external domain, and FS-01.

mentor.stage_hint: Select the external C2 domain first, validate DNS-SRV as the control point, then confirm the compromised host and staged data risk.
mentor.coverage_incomplete: Final containment is not ready yet. Validate external C2, DNS-SRV, WS-SALES-01, and FS-01 before response.
mentor.wrong_order: Blocking before confirming the active C2 path and staged data risk weakens the final report.
mentor.premature_response: A final block should follow evidence that the domain path is part of the active campaign.
mentor.correct_sequence: Good sequence. You validated the active C2 path and staged data risk before blocking the malicious domain.
mentor.timeout_warning: Time pressure is critical. Delayed containment may allow staged data exfiltration.
mentor.timeout_feedback: The delay increased data-loss exposure and degraded the final scenario outcome.

correct.mentor_feedback: The DNS C2 path was validated and blocked before staged data could leave the network.
correct.log_message: External C2 domain and DNS control point blocked after coordinated containment validation.

wrong.mentor_feedback: Failure to block the active C2 channel leaves staged data at risk of outbound transfer.
wrong.log_message: DNS C2 channel remains active and exfiltration risk persists.

ai_metadata.stage_objective: Apply coordinated containment by validating the external C2 domain, DNS control point, compromised workstation, and staged data risk before blocking the malicious DNS path.

facts.label: The external C2 path should be validated before blocking.
The compromised workstation should be confirmed before final containment.
Final response should coordinate DNS/path blocking with host and data-risk awareness.
